method: Primary-source reading and comparison with local atlas events. Corporate outcome claims retain attribution; experimental results, surveys, contracts and theoretical models are distinguished. No independent replication or economy-wide bubble valuation was performed.

sources.finding: AIFS entered operations alongside IFS with 24/7 support.
sources.locator: Opening paragraph; Further plans, statement by Director of Forecasts and Services
sources.limit: Operational deployment does not measure provider profitability or economy-wide productivity.

sources.finding: Google reports recovery of an average 0.7% of worldwide compute through a scheduling heuristic already in production for over a year.
sources.limit: Company measurement; not independently replicated here; not a 0.7% profit or energy-saving metric.

sources.finding: Klarna reports 80% of support chats, workload equivalent to over 850 agents, approximately USD 59 million annual savings, and continued access to human support.
sources.locator: AI-driven efficiency, paragraphs beginning 'We announced a partnership with OpenAI in 2023'
sources.limit: Management estimates, not an independently audited causal AI effect. Workload equivalence is not a dismissal count. Filing date needs confirmation before event creation.

sources.finding: 758 participants; within-frontier tasks improved on completion and time metrics, while the outside-frontier task produced a roughly 19 percentage-point reduction in correctness with AI.
sources.locator: Abstract; Outside the Frontier, Figure 5 and Table 7; discussion referencing September 2023 working paper
sources.limit: GPT-4-era experiment, not a 2026 model evaluation. Only one outside-frontier task. Abstract's 19% shorthand is clarified as percentage points in the main text.

sources.finding: Time horizon pairs human-expert task duration with a specified probability of agent success; the page distinguishes 50% and 80% thresholds.
sources.locator: Definition; Methodological Details; FAQ on autonomous duration; Task distribution
sources.limit: Not elapsed autonomous working time or a general employee replacement metric; mainly software, ML and cyber tasks. Page no longer actively updated.

sources.finding: Almost 6000 executives across four countries; 89% average share reporting no productivity impact over the preceding three years.
sources.locator: Introduction on fieldwork; section 4.4, printed page 15, Figure 10
sources.limit: Retrospective self-reports; productivity means sales volume per employee. Does not describe November 2026 model performance.

sources.finding: Kicinski reports overload, longstanding API races exposed by LLMs, and Meta-supported budget/access for multi-model review.
sources.locator: Opening paragraphs before Networking changes for 7.3
sources.limit: No causal aggregate productivity estimate. Counts 632/648 describe patches, not AI-discovered vulnerabilities. Sponsor control of the project is not established.

sources.finding: Studied cloud-AI partnerships include commitments to spend a large portion of investor funding on the investor's cloud services.
sources.limit: Studied partnerships, not every AI contract; interconnected funding is not proof of fictitious revenue.

sources.finding: Contract value up to USD 11.9 billion, together with issuance of USD 350 million CoreWeave stock to OpenAI.
sources.limit: Contract ceiling, not recognized revenue or cash received; historical deal, not the total current relationship.

sources.finding: Supply relationships accompany 16.1% by count and 46.4% by value of AI-to-AI investment deals in the study.
sources.limit: Denominator is AI-to-AI investment deals, not sector revenue or all capital expenditure.

sources.finding: Around 20% of planned data-centre projects risk delays without remedies; new transmission lines take four to eight years in advanced economies.
sources.locator: Smarter is faster when it comes to integrating data centres in electricity grids
sources.limit: Conditional risk estimate for data centres generally, not observed cancellations or an AI-only share.
sources.source_hygiene_note: Existing executive-summary URL ends with encoded NBSP (%C2%A0); clean URL used here. Atlas not edited.

sources.finding: USD 45.2 billion capex; roughly three quarters short-lived assets, primarily CPUs/GPUs; USD 18.6 billion company-wide free cash flow.
sources.locator: Amy Hood prepared remarks, capital expenditures and cash flow
sources.limit: Company-wide metrics. Capex including finance-lease recognition differs from cash PP&E payments; FCF does not establish standalone AI profitability.

sources.finding: Maps SPV, lease and guarantee exposures; observed broad bond-market spillovers were small and short-lived.
sources.locator: Key takeaways; Emerging credit relationships; Spillovers from AI borrowing
sources.limit: Market event associations are not causal effects. The paper does not establish an ongoing systemic crisis.

sources.finding: Competition for dominant market positions can produce aggregate overinvestment under the model's assumptions.
sources.limit: Model output is not measured excess physical capacity. Numerical excess-investment estimates are deliberately omitted from the article.

sources.finding: EO 14320 directs support for full-stack AI export packages using financial and diplomatic tools within legal authority and appropriations.
sources.limit: Policy direction does not establish disbursements, completed exports or buyer dependence in a specific country.

sources.finding: Less than 1% annual customer switching and sustained AWS/Microsoft cloud returns above cost of capital in the investigated market.
sources.locator: Summary paragraphs 8, 24; technical and licensing barriers sections
sources.limit: Cloud-market findings are not a measure of whole-AI-market profitability or proof all customer retention is involuntary.

sources.finding: Transfer-cost measures improved exit terms, with limited uptake and continuing IAM and cloud-specific Kubernetes portability barriers.
sources.limit: Some barriers improved; no measured elimination of lock-in. Do not report every measure as first launched in October.

sources.finding: MoD justifies planned GBP 240.6 million direct award through architecture rebuilding, reaccreditation, retraining and disruption from changing supplier.
sources.limit: Buyer's justification, not independent cost measurement. This notice precedes signature; article does not treat December 18 as contract-signing date.

analysis.hypothesis: Useful AI applications, financial overcommitment and durable supplier power can coexist; none establishes the other automatically.

tests.risk_rises_if: Demand contracts when fresh financing or cloud credits stop
tests.risk_falls_if: Renewals persist without subsidy and cover full service costs

tests.risk_rises_if: Review and correction queues absorb task-level savings
tests.risk_falls_if: End-to-end cost and time fall at stable quality

tests.risk_rises_if: Binding costs start before paying utilization
tests.risk_falls_if: Operating cash covers operations, financing and refresh

tests.risk_rises_if: One counterparty supports several correlated revenue, collateral and guarantee claims
tests.risk_falls_if: Loss of the counterparty is absorbable without cascading defaults

tests.risk_rises_if: Alternative models leave expensive platform migration
tests.risk_falls_if: Customers migrate with predictable cost, time and functional continuity

tests.risk_rises_if: Withdrawal of support removes both demand and autonomous operational value
tests.risk_falls_if: A funded, tested strategic function or sustainable paid service persists

scenarios_not_facts: Financial repricing may concentrate assets and customers among stronger suppliers.
Excess capacity and practical portability may instead intensify competition and lower prices.
